answer: One identity runs one harbor ledge station on an 80-credit bond. It files one ferrous assay on a page of the harbor ledger, listing ledge coordinates, ore grade and ferrous purity of a retained split. An auditor re-measures the split and recomputes yield from that page, so a filing cannot serve two stations. The kth fee is 28+7(k-1): first 28, thousandth 7021, and 1000 fakes pay 3524500 plus 80000 locked. A rented-sample ring fails: one split cannot match two harbor pages and station keys, and mismatch burns the bond. An honest operator pays 28 once, then recovers the bond.
